problem: The densities quoted are not standard steam-table values: water is about 992 kg/m³ at 40 °C and about 972 kg/m³ at 80 °C. 995 kg/m³ is closer to 30 °C and 977 kg/m³ to 75 °C. The method and arithmetic are correct, but a student who memorises these numbers will carry a small error forward.
fix: Either label them as illustrative round figures, or use 992 kg/m³ and 972 kg/m³. Then Δρ = 20 kg/m³ and Δp = 20 × 9.81 × 0.4 = 78.48 Pa (about 78.5 Pa).

problem: The trap 'A pressure cap raises the boiling point; it does not increase cooling capacity' sits awkwardly against Section 2, which says hotter coolant lets the radiator be smaller. A student will read the two as contradicting each other.
fix: Word the trap as: 'A pressure cap removes no heat itself. It raises the boiling margin so the coolant can run hotter; the extra heat rejection comes from the larger coolant-to-air temperature difference, not from the cap.'

problem: The blocks are laid out downwards with the jacket first, so the radiator appears below the jacket. The text and the aria label say hot water rises from the jacket to the radiator, so the picture contradicts the physics.
fix: Put the radiator at the top and the jacket at the bottom: jacket → riser going up → radiator → downcomer coming down → jacket. Set the direction so the riser is shown above the jacket.
